kernelIdea: |z| = √(a² + b²) is the distance from 0; |z| = √(z z̄); it extends absolute value on ℝ; |z − w| is the distance between z and w, and |z − w| = r describes a circle.

kernels.l1: How far from home? Measure it with a piece of string.
kernels.l2: To find how far a spot is from the start, use the across part and the up part and make a right triangle. The slanted side is the distance.
kernels.l3: The modulus |z| is the distance from 0 to z, and Pythagoras gives |a + bi| = √(a² + b²). For ordinary numbers it is just the usual distance from zero.
kernels.l4: |z| = √(a² + b²) = √(z z̄) is the distance from the origin to z; it agrees with absolute value on ℝ, |z − w| is the distance between z and w, and |z − w| = r describes a circle.
kernels.l5: The modulus is the Euclidean distance to the origin; distances, circles, and disks in ℂ are all described by inequalities in |z − w|.
kernels.l6: Modulus is a norm on ℂ: it is multiplicative and satisfies the triangle inequality, making ℂ a metric space in which analysis can be done.
kernels.l7: |z| = √(z z̄) is the Euclidean distance from 0, extends absolute value on ℝ, satisfies |zw| = |z||w| and the triangle inequality, and turns |z − w| = r into a circle.
kernels.l8: Modulus is the norm making ℂ a complete normed field; multiplicativity is the norm of the quadratic extension, and completeness is what makes complex analysis possible.
